title: Finite-field sheaf model for an algebraic-closure direct image
statement: Fix a prime ell and a characteristic-p field k, with p prime and p != ell. Let X and Y be separated finite-type k-schemes and f:X -> Y a k-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Use the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], stratified locally finitely presented constructible module objects [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and the ordinary ambient derived direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let Qbar_ell be the algebraic-closure coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For each constructible Qbar_ell,X-module F there exist a finite intermediate extension E/Q_ell inside Qbar_ell, a constructible E_X-module N, and an isomorphism L(Qbar_ell,Y tensor_{E_Y} -)(Rf_{*,E}(N[0])) ~= Rf_{*,Qbar_ell}(F[0]). Here the coefficient inclusion is [def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map]. No upper bound for either direct image is part of this statement.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X locally Noetherian, and the quasi-compact structural map makes X compact. Hence X is Noetherian. Apply exists_constructible_finiteCoefficient_model to F, obtaining a finite intermediate field E, a constructible E-module N and an isomorphism of the ordinary scalar extension of N with F. This is directly sheaf descent; no derived model or truncation is needed.

Flat algebraic-closure scalar extension is exact. Apply singleFunctorCompLeftDerivedFunctorIso to identify its left derived functor on N[0] with the single complex of its ordinary extension, and compose with the single functor applied to the descended sheaf isomorphism. This gives L(extension)(N[0]) isomorphic to F[0].

Separatedness of the structural map gives a quasi-separated target space. Compactness of X and Noetherianity give QuasiCompact f and QuasiSeparated f. The single complex N[0] lies in D-plus with lower bound zero. Apply isIso_derivedPushHom_padicAlgCl_of_boundedBelow to this object. Turn the canonical coefficient-change map into an isomorphism and compose it with Rf_* of the isomorphism of the preceding step. The result is exactly the asserted scalar-extension model for the direct image.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.4(3); Proposition 6.8.14; Remark 6.8.15; finite-stage paragraph; direct sheaf descent via the existing finite-presentation descent theorem, followed by the bounded-below coefficient-change mate
